questions.stem: Which among the following leads to detachment of Myosin head from Actin?

options.label: B
options.text: Attachment of ATP on Myosin Head

questions.answerText: Attachment of ATP on Myosin Head
questions.solutionHtml:
Attachment of ATP on Myosin Head

The detachment of the myosin head from actin occurs when ATP (adenosine triphosphate) binds to the myosin head.



Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no 103,104,105, Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 25th Edition, Page Number:99.

questions.stem: Counter current mechanism seen in which of the following ?SkinKidneyTestsIntestinesSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1,2,3,4
  • Counter current mechanism is seen in all 4 sites given, i.e., skin, kidney, testes and intestines.
  • Statement: 1 and 3: In skin and testes, it helps in temperature regulation (Countercurrent Heat Exchange).
  • Blood flowing from the core to the periphery (like the legs & feet) carries heat that can be readily lost through the skin. Similarly for testis, blood that returns from the testes through the plexuses is cooler than the blood in testicular arteries. The arterial blood is cooled by venous blood by a counter-current heat exchange mechanism.
  • Statement: 4: In the Intestine it helps in better absorption of nutrients.
  • Statement: 2: In the kidney it helps in maintaining the Hyperosmolarity of Medullary interstitium. The nephrons involved in the formation of concentrated urine extend all the way from the cortex of the kidney to the medulla and are accompanied by vasa recta.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 25th Edition, Page Number:642

questions.stem: What will happen to the alveolar ventilation when pH is changed from 7.4 to 7.3 at PaO2 100 mmHg ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased Ventilation

When the pH of the blood changes, it affects the body's acid-base balance, leading to respiratory compensation. Specifically, a decrease in pH (from 7.4 to 7.3 in this case) indicates a condition of acidosis, and the body will attempt to compensate for this by increasing ventilation.



Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition page no. 617, Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 25th Edition, Page Number:610

questions.stem: Which of the following act by increasing phospholipase C?
questions.solutionHtml:
Gq
  • Gq is a type of G protein that activates phospholipase C (PLC). When a G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) activates Gq, it promotes the activation of PLC, which in turn catalyzes the hydrolysis of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) to produce inositol trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG).
  • These secondary messengers, IP3, and DAG, are involved in various cellular signaling pathways.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 25th Edition, Page Number:54.

questions.stem: Two vessels one with diameter D and length L. Another with diameter 2D and length 2L. The rate of flow in second will be how many times that of first?
questions.solutionHtml:
8 Times
  • F= ΔP x π/8 x 1/ η x r4/L, where
  • F = flow
  • ΔP = pressure difference between two ends of the tube
  • η= viscosity
  • r = radius of the tube
  • L = length of the tube
  • Flow through B = (2*r)4/2L = 8 times


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 25th Edition, Page Number: 541.

questions.stem: Wrong one among the following about accommodation changes in high altitude ascent is ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Respiratory Acidosis
  • The physiological adaptation that does not happen at high altitudes is respiratory acidosis.
  • Respiratory alkalosis is the physiological adaptation seen at high altitudes due to hyperventilation and not respiratory acidosis.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 25th Edition, Page Number:611. Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no 637, 638, 639, Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no 554-556, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no 3333.
